title: Vulnerability telemetry, RBAC v2 & SIEM export — evidence automation design
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a proposed design to unify vulnerability scanner outputs, RBAC v2 enforcement on evidence access, an enriched audit-log schema for downstream compliance, and a SIEM export mapping (Elastic/CEF/Syslog) to support automated remediation tracking and SLAs. The intent is a pragmatic, incremental rollout that preserves compatibility with existing triage dashboards while enabling stronger access controls and auditable evidence handoffs.

Background and motivation:
- Current situation: multiple scanners (internal container-scan, oss-dep-scan, infra-scanner) produce CSV/JSON artifacts that are stored in S3 and referenced in Jira tickets. Evidence access is coarse-grained (S3 perms). Audit logs are sparse (file read events, ticket comments).
- Problems: lack of unified event schema, no consistent RBAC enforcement for who can append evidence or mark remediation, SIEM lacks normalized fields for vulnerability events, and automation for patch/evidence proof is brittle.

Goals:
1) Define an audit/event schema for vulnerability lifecycle events (scanner-discovery -> triage -> evidence-add -> remediation-verify).
2) Enforce RBAC v2 controls on evidence and actioning (who can set patch-state, who can mark evidence as verified).
3) Build a SIEM export mapping (Elastic ECS first, with CEF fallback for QRadar) that contains the necessary fields for SLA dashboards and forensic investigations.
4) Automate evidence ingestion and ticket updates to reduce manual handoffs and accelerate MTTR.

Non-goals:
- Replacing existing scanner engines.
- Full rewrite of triage UI in this phase.

High-level architecture (proposed):
1) Scanner pipeline: scanners emit normalized "vuln_discovery" events to an intermediate event bus (Kafka). Event enrichment service attaches asset metadata (owner, team, workload_id), computes canonical vuln_id (scanner + fingerprint), resolves CVE metadata from internal DB.
2) Evidence store: immutable object store with per-object ACLs managed by RBAC v2 service. Objects are referenced by evidence_id in events. Evidence lifecycle events are audit-logged.
3) Audit event log: append-only audit topic capturing every state change. Audit producer libraries used in triage UI, automation runners, evidence-API.
4) SIEM bridge: subscribes to audit topic, transforms events into Elastic ECS documents and CEF records for export.
5) Remediation automation: workflows (Playbooks) that can open/transition tickets, push deployment patches, and append automated evidence proofs (e.g., package-lock hash updates, deployment run IDs).

RBAC v2: roles & permission matrix (proposal):
- system:scanner (service principal) — permissions: create:vuln_discovery, attach:evidence (but only within scanner-owned namespace), read:vuln_meta
- vuln-reader — read:vuln_meta, read:evidence (redacted), comment:ticket
- vuln-triage — all vuln-reader perms + update:triage_state, assign:vuln, add:evidence (non-destructive), request-remediation
- evidence-admin — create/append evidence, delete-evidence (soft delete), manage-evidence-tags
- remediation-approver — approve remediation verification, set:remediation_state=verified
- sec-auditor — read:all (audit-only; evidence content redacted), export:siem_feed
Notes: RBAC v2 will be enforced by a centralized authorization service (token introspection + fine-grained policy) on the evidence API and the triage API.

Audit log / event schema (v1): top-level required fields
- event_id: string (uuid)
- event_type: string (vuln_discovery | triage_update | evidence_added | evidence_access | remediation_state_change)
- timestamp: iso8601
- actor_id: string (user id or service principal)
- actor_role: string (from RBAC v2 role set)
- vuln_id: string (canonical id)
- severity: string (critical|high|medium|low|info)
- source_scanner: string (scanner name/version)
- asset: string (asset id, e.g., instance/container/image id)
- evidence_ids: list of strings (comma-separated in CSV if needed)
- change_summary: string (human readable)
- prev_state: string
- new_state: string
- trace_id: string (correlate across systems)
- raw_payload_url: string (signed URL to original scanner payload; access controlled)

Example audit event (text):
{
  "event_id": "e7f2a3c0-9b1d-4d2e-9aef-1234567890ab",
  "event_type": "evidence_added",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-14T18:12:23Z",
  "actor_id": "svc:container-scanner",
  "actor_role": "system:scanner",
  "vuln_id": "scannerX-20260914-9f3a1",
  "severity": "high",
  "source_scanner": "container-scan-3.2.1",
  "asset": "i-0abcd1234ef567890",
  "evidence_ids": "evid-20260914-55",
  "change_summary": "uploaded SBOM fragment and patch-proof",
  "trace_id": "t-59a0d2c3",
  "raw_payload_url": "s3://sec-evidence/prod/2026/09/14/scan-9f3a1.json"
}

SIEM export mapping (Elastic ECS preferred):
- index: security-vulnerabilities-YYYY.MM
- ecs fields mapping (proposed):
  - event.category = "vulnerability"
  - event.type = event_type
  - event.dataset = "redwood.vuln"
  - event.id = event_id
  - event.created = timestamp
  - host.id = asset
  - vulnerability.id = vuln_id
  - vulnerability.severity = severity
  - vulnerability.scanner.vendor = source_scanner
  - user.id = actor_id
  - user.roles = actor_role
  - file.hash.sha256 = evidence_content_hash (if provided)
  - url.original = raw_payload_url
  - tags = [ "vuln:managed", "team:platform" ]
Notes for CEF/QRadar: map event.id -> cn1, vulnerability.severity -> severity, include extension fields: ext.vulnId, ext.asset, ext.evidenceIds. Provide a compact CEF mapping for legacy consumers.

Evidence automation flow (detailed):
1) Scanner emits vuln_discovery event -> Kafka topic.
2) Enrichment lambda attaches asset and ownership -> writes normalized event to vuln_topic.
3) Automation rules evaluate severity + ownership -> if auto-patch eligible, enqueue playbook run.
4) Playbook runs against infra pipelines, produces evidence proof (deployment-run-id, image-digest). Playbook writes evidence object to evidence-store and emits evidence_added event.
5) Evidence_added triggers SIEM bridge and a ticket update (attach evidence link + set remediation_state=patching).
6) Post-deploy verification step compares expected hashes and sets remediation_state=verified or failed.

Patch SLA tracking and KPIs (for dashboards):
- Mean time to triage (MTTTriage) — time from vuln_discovery -> triage_state != "untriaged"
- Mean time to remediation start (MTTRStart) — discovery -> remediation_state=patching
- Mean time to remediation verified (MTTRVerified) — discovery -> remediation_state=verified
- Percent auto-remediated within SLA (e.g., 72h)
- Evidence completeness ratio (vulns with proof attached / total vuls)

Operational concerns and constraints:
- Data retention: audit topic retained 2 years; SIEM indices retained per compliance (1 year hot, 3 years cold). Raw scanner payloads retention limited to 90 days unless explicitly flagged.
- Redaction: evidence content may contain PII or secrets; evidence API performs automated scanning and redaction before storing; audit logs must not contain full secret values.
- RBAC enforcement latency: microsecond-level checks are required on hot paths; evaluate policy caching strategies.
- Scale: peak scanner throughput ~20k events/min. SIEM bridge must bulk transform and compress to meet ingest quotas.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): specification and small PoC — produce canonical event, single scanner -> Kafka -> Elastic index.
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): build evidence-store ACLs + RBAC integration; enforce RBAC on evidence-API; wire in triage UI hooks.
- Phase 2 (6 weeks): SIEM bridge full mapping (ECS + CEF), playbook integration for auto-patch for non-customer-facing infra.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): expand to OSS dependency scanner, add RBAC fine-tunes, run compliance audit.

Open questions / action items:
- Q1: Which teams should be in the initial remediation-approver group? (action: security product to propose list by 2026-09-21)
- Q2: Can existing S3 ACLs be progressively migrated to evidence-store without breaking links in Jira? (action: infra to prototype signed URL passthrough)
- Q3: How to represent aggregated vulnerabilities (same CVE across multiple assets) in the canonical vuln_id model? (action: design a mapping rule set)
- Q4: Decide retention policy harmonization between audit-topic and SIEM index (security/legal)

Appendix A — sample events (two examples):
1) vuln_discovery sample:
{
  "event_id": "d3f1c8a2-4a2b-4c3c-8b2f-0a1b2c3d4e5f",
  "event_type": "vuln_discovery",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-14T17:01:05Z",
  "actor_id": "svc:oss-dep-scan",
  "actor_role": "system:scanner",
  "vuln_id": "oss-npm-20260914-44",
  "severity": "medium",
  "source_scanner": "oss-dep-scan-1.9",
  "asset": "pkg:github/redwood/inference@1.3.2",
  "raw_payload_url": "s3://sec-scans/oss/2026/09/14/oss-44.json",
  "trace_id": "t-88ab22"
}

2) remediation_state_change sample:
{
  "event_id": "f6a2b5e4-7f5a-4a1e-b2c3-6e4f5d8c7b9a",
  "event_type": "remediation_state_change",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-14T20:05:10Z",
  "actor_id": "u:priya.shah@redwood.ai",
  "actor_role": "remediation-approver",
  "vuln_id": "scannerX-20260914-9f3a1",
  "prev_state": "patching",
  "new_state": "verified",
  "change_summary": "verified deployment run 2026-09-14-457 with expected image-digest",
  "evidence_ids": "evid-20260914-55",
  "trace_id": "t-59a0d2c3"
}

Notes on uniqueness: This doc focuses on an integrated telemetry-first design that explicitly ties RBAC v2 enforcement to evidence ACLs, a normalized audit schema optimized for Elastic ECS and CEF outputs, and an end-to-end automation flow that surfaces evidence proofs into triage tickets and the SIEM. It intentionally avoids duplicating scanner-only outputs and provides actionable rollout steps and KPIs.

Next steps (owner: Asha): finalize schema and policy draft, circulate to infra and product, schedule PoC sprint with infra (start 2026-09-21).
